task_1.title: Fix uncached downloads without SHA-256
task_1.description: Conan 2.28.1 fixes a regression where downloads requested without a SHA-256 checksum could interact incorrectly with source caching and alternate source-origin handling. Such downloads must remain allowed, but they cannot safely participate in checksum-based cache behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that downloads requested without a SHA-256 checksum still complete from their original URL when source caching behavior is configured, while avoiding unsafe cache use.

expectation.grounded: When conan.tools.files.download() is handled by SourcesCachingDownloader with an active download cache folder and no sha256 checksum, it must warn that caching cannot be used for that download, disable cache participation for that download, and restrict the active source origin list to origin. Existing behavior for checksum-protected downloads, absolute-path validation of core.sources:download_cache, and ConanException handling for invalid active source-origin values must remain intact.
expectation.conceptual: A download without a checksum should behave as a direct, uncached download from the requested source. Cache and backup-source features must not turn the missing checksum into a failed or redirected download, and users should receive a warning when caching was requested but cannot be used.

constraints.grounded: Do not cache artifacts for download() calls that lack sha256. Do not use configured alternate source origins after cache handling has been disabled because sha256 is absent; use only origin for that download. Preserve normal cache and source-origin behavior for downloads that provide sha256, and preserve existing configuration validation outside the no-checksum cache-disabled path.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must avoid storing unverifiable downloads and must not alter normal cached-download behavior for checksum-protected downloads or unrelated configuration validation.

behavior: When source caching is configured and a download has no SHA-256 checksum, the downloader emits a warning and treats the download as non-cacheable.
For the same no-checksum path, configured source-origin alternatives are ignored and the downloader uses only the original URL source.
Downloads without a checksum are still allowed to proceed instead of failing solely because source caching or alternate source origins are configured.
Downloads with a checksum continue to use existing cache and source-origin behavior.
Configuration validation for non-absolute cache paths and invalid active source-origin entries remains unchanged outside the no-checksum cache-disabled path.
acceptance_criteria: Given a download request without sha256 and source caching configured, when the download is executed, it should warn that caching cannot be used, avoid using the download cache for that request, and fetch from the original source.

Given alternate source origins are configured and the current download has no sha256 while cache handling is disabled for that reason, when the downloader selects origins, it should use only the original source.
Given a download request that includes sha256, when cache and source-origin configuration are present, it should continue to participate in the existing cached and alternate-source workflow.
Given an invalid non-absolute core.sources:download_cache path, when caching is otherwise active, it should still raise the existing ConanException.

Given active source-origin configuration containing invalid None values outside the no-checksum cache-disabled case, when the downloader validates origins, it should still raise the existing ConanException.
